candidate_relations.reason: Muscle invasive aspergillosis is an invasive fungal infection anatomically consistent with the MRI findings, but asserts Aspergillus as the causative organism, which conflicts with the reference diagnosis of Mucormycosis. Negative galactomannan and the clinical context (agricultural worker, neutropenia, cystic necrotic lesion) favor Mucor over Aspergillus.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Invasive fungal infection of muscle but specifies Aspergillus rather than Mucor

candidate_relations.reason: Pyomyositis describes bacterial suppurative muscle infection and could explain the cystic necrotic intramuscular lesion, but it does not capture the fungal (Mucor) etiology that is the reference diagnosis. It is a differential rather than the final diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Bacterial muscle infection; does not capture fungal etiology

candidate_relations.reason: Mastocytosis is a mast cell neoplasm with no relevance to the infectious/fungal presentation described in this immunocompromised patient.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Mast cell proliferative disorder; unrelated to the clinical scenario

candidate_relations.reason: Invasive Fungal Infection is the parent category that includes Mucormycosis, but it does not specify the organism. It is compatible but missing the required specificity of the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Correct category (invasive fungal infection) but lacks organism-level specificity (Mucormycosis)

candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record clearly documents B-cell ALL (TdT, CD34, CD19, CD10, CD22, HLA-DR positive). AML is a different diagnostic entity and is not the requested diagnosis (Mucormycosis).
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Wrong leukemia subtype; the underlying malignancy is ALL, not AML

candidate_relations.reason: Muscle abscess describes the morphological/radiological finding (cystic necrotic lesion) but does not specify the fungal etiology (Mucormycosis). It is a manifestation/complication rather than the final etiologic diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Describes the anatomical finding (abscess) rather than the etiologic diagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: Erdheim-Chester Disease is a non-Langerhans histiocytosis with no relevance to the infectious presentation in this neutropenic patient.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Rare histiocytic disorder; entirely unrelated to the clinical scenario

candidate_relations.reason: Contact dermatitis refers to the eczematous plaques that resolved with topical steroids and is explicitly not the diagnosis being sought. It is unrelated to Mucormycosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Skin condition already treated and resolved; not the requested diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Negative galactomannan supports Mucormycosis over Aspergillosis; agricultural exposure and cystic necrotic muscle lesion in a profoundly neutropenic patient are classic Mucor risk factors

Eczematous plaques on chest and proximal right arm in proximity to the eventual muscle lesion site may represent early cutaneous Mucormycosis rather than contact dermatitis, though this is not definitively stated
